triage sets everything about an issue other than its state: its owner, the
epic it belongs to, what it waits on, and its priority.

It writes a triage/<id> branch for a pull request, like everything else here.
--push writes straight to trunk instead, and is refused unless .isu.yml sets
direct_triage: true — the field is how a team says out loud that triage is not a
code review.

The body and any keys isu does not know survive byte for byte. This rewrites the
lines it was asked to and nothing else.

Usage:
  isu triage <id> [flags]

Flags:
      --blocked-by strings   the issues it waits on, replacing what is there
  -h, --help                 help for triage
      --owner string         the human answerable for it
      --parent string        the epic it belongs to
      --priority string      p0, p1, p2 or p3
      --push                 commit straight to trunk instead of onto a branch

Global Flags:
      --fetch         update remote refs before reading
      --json          print newline-delimited JSON instead of text
      --no-color      never colour the output
      --ref string    the ref isu treats as trunk (default: main, else master, else HEAD)
      --repo string   the repository to read (default: the working directory)
